audience_desire: Stay independent, avoid a fall that ends mobility
evidence: Median outlier multiple 1.67x, 40% outlier rate (n=20) - highest of any internally taxonomy'd cluster except Digestion. Broke out independently on 2 unrelated channels (Doctor Thomas 122x, Dr. Aliza Wright 1009x) within days of each other.
trend_evidence: Google Trends 'balance exercises for seniors' stable evergreen 50-90 range, no seasonality — durable demand, not a fad.
psychology: Fear of loss of independence + hope/reversibility ('one simple change')
risk: Cross-channel proven, still not fully saturated internally (only 20 of 306 videos)

audience_desire: Feel lighter, resolve embarrassing/uncomfortable symptoms cheaply and naturally
evidence: Median outlier multiple 1.75x, 46% outlier rate (n=26) - highest internal cluster. 'Clove' sub-cluster alone is 40 videos on one channel with massive external market validation (5.9M/2.6M/1M+ view videos from unrelated creators).
trend_evidence: Google Trends 'clove water' evergreen with a Feb-2026 peak (~100) that predates this channel's biggest hit by 2 months — trend contribution plausible but not sole cause.
psychology: Curiosity ('what happens in 10 minutes'), natural-remedy trust, low cost/no medication
risk: Highly execution-dependent — most videos in this cluster underperform (median still only 1.75x); requires strong curiosity-gap packaging every time

audience_desire: Avoid sudden, catastrophic heart event; reassurance through vigilance
evidence: Bimodal: matched pairs show specific-mechanism titles (stroke/sleeping position, 32x) beat generic-advice titles (safest blood pressure, 0.15x) on the SAME channel repeatedly.
trend_evidence: Not deep-Trends-researched this pass; evergreen health-news topic by general knowledge, needs verification before launch.
psychology: Fear of hidden danger + authority (cardiologist framing)
risk: Most-covered topic across all 6 competitors (70 of 306 videos) but weakest median performance (0.80x) — high competition, needs sharp differentiation

audience_desire: Avoid being harmed by their own prescriptions; feel informed vs their doctor
evidence: Matched pair: naming specific drugs (Losartan/Amlodipine/Metoprolol) in title outperformed (216x) vs single-drug generic framing (0.14x) on same channel.
psychology: Distrust of pharma/medical system, specificity signals credibility
risk: MEDICAL SAFETY: must not suggest stopping medication; frame as 'ask your doctor about' not medical advice

audience_desire: Catch silent disease before it becomes serious
evidence: One EXTREME_BREAKOUT (2485x) from a near-dormant channel (median 199 views), but exact same script/title reused verbatim by 2 other tiny channels got only 20-36 views each. Topic itself has low median performance (0.75x) internally.
trend_evidence: Google Trends 'diabetic foot signs' sparse/noisy, low baseline volume — not strong evergreen search demand at this specific phrase.
risk: Single outlier may be algorithm-luck (POSSIBLE RECOMMENDATION-EXPANSION, not proven repeatable) — treat as experiment, not core pillar

audience_desire: Simple food swaps that protect organ health
evidence: Highly inconsistent — near-identical title template ('Your Kidneys Are Begging You to Eat These N Foods') scored 56.9x on one video and 0.23x on another on the same channel — title template alone is not sufficient.
risk: Confirmed negative evidence against relying on title template alone — needs additional differentiator (specificity, story, visual proof) beyond the template
